title: Instructions For Correct Assembly - review
transcript: instructions for correct assembly Anu played by Thomas cycle share directed by Hamish Perry at Royal Court Theatre London so if there were instructions for the correct assembly of a stage play how would they read first we've got a good theme here we have to dealing with grief and when we create something how much responsibility and control do we have then you need a plot again we have to we start with a married couple who enjoy DIY constructing a human it becomes apparent that they're trying to create an improved version of their young adult son who died the second story of what happened to their son is told in parallel the two don't always fit easily together because the sci-fi story leads to some hilarious moments as the robot tries to please but reveals his essential a morality some so rude I can't repeat them here while the other story is poignant sometimes brutal in its portrayal of what it's like when your child is an addict then you need good characters and you need to assemble a cast of good actors to play them well Jane Horrocks and Mark Bonner are excellent as the fragile that positive parents Brian vernal is brilliant both as the son and a specialist who's fast talking robot replacement neither son turns out how the parents plan and this is the glue that holds the play together but as with many assembly pacts there is one piece missing a heart funny and interesting as it was I didn't find the play emotionally involving nevertheless I give instructions or correct assembly for stars if you found this review interesting you may like to see a more detailed version on my website 1-minute theater reviews coda UK
